chapter: Chano Pozo, Town Hall and Charlie Parker
title: Never a record collector
summary: Machito says he kept few of his records because his children and friends gave them away and he never thought of himself as a genius.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: You did it at the Concord. Okay, Macho, do you have a copy of all these things you did?
No, not many because I never really, I never was a record collector.
You mean to say that after you recorded something, you and Mario never made an effort to pick up one of those 78s?
We have all the amount that any artist could have, but my children used to give it away; and friends -

somebody come along - "Hey, Machito, I like that". Here, here, because to us seems like they would never stop to produce those records or release those records, or, I don't know, we -- it was good records and we liked it, but we never thought that we was inventing a refreshment or - but we didn't consider ourselves a science or nothing, whatever. I mean, a musician that enjoyed what we were doing and we know what we were doing because everything was planned, but we never give it that importance to consider ourselves a genius ....
